Appendix DLP · Witness Resolvents · The Metaplectic Prime and the \(Z\)-Condensation Split

Where this sits. DKO recovered a hidden residue by passing to the complex that actually manufactures it rather than reading it off a package. The witness-spin experiment of Takahashi–Murphy–Wood-Thanan–…–Flicker–Davis (Nat. Phys. 2026; herbertsmithite) is the physical cousin of that move: a degree of freedom dismissed as impurity is reread as a probe whose dynamics factor through the hidden medium’s response kernel. framing The object that survives translation into this monograph is not an identity between spinons and arithmetic torsion; it is a kernel. In the modular-categorical specialization the kernel is exact and finite, and that is what this appendix certifies.

For a modular tensor category \(\mathcal C\) with simple objects \(a\in\operatorname{Irr}(\mathcal C)\), \(S\)-matrix \(S_{ab}\), and a chosen witness object \(W\), the vacuum witness moments are \(m_n(W)=\dim\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbf 1,W^{\otimes n})=(N_W^{\,n})_{\mathbf 1\mathbf 1}\), where \(N_W\) is the fusion matrix. The generating function is the witness resolvent \(R_W(z)=\sum_{n\ge0}m_n(W)\,z^n\). Verlinde diagonalization \(N_W=S\operatorname{diag}(S_{Wa}/S_{0a})S^{-1}\) gives the closed rational form \[ R_W(z)=\big[(I-zN_W)^{-1}\big]_{\mathbf 1\mathbf 1}=\sum_{a}\frac{S_{0a}^{2}}{1-z\,S_{Wa}/S_{0a}}, \] a finite rational function whose poles are the witness eigenvalues \(\lambda_a=S_{Wa}/S_{0a}\). The Verlinde formula and the braid-fusion functor \(F_W:\mathsf{Br}\to\mathcal C\) underneath this are imported; the closed-form identity, and the Fibonacci \(R_\tau=(1-z)/(1-z-z^2)\) and Ising \(R_\sigma=(1-z^2)/(1-2z^2)\) instances, are checked in-sandbox to exact arithmetic. verified

The first nontrivial target is the odd Tambara–Yamagami sector \(\operatorname{TY}(\mathbf Z/p)\), whose noninvertible object obeys \(\sigma\otimes a=\sigma\) for \(a\in\mathbf Z/p\) and \(\sigma\otimes\sigma=\bigoplus_{a\in\mathbf Z/p}a\). The fusion matrix is the bipartite block \(\binom{0\ \ \mathbf 1}{\mathbf 1^{\!\top}\ 0}\), and its even powers feed the all-ones block \(J_p\) with \(J_p^{\,k}=p^{\,k-1}J_p\), forcing the moments and resolvent below.

TY witness-prime theoremVerified · fusion-level

For \(\operatorname{TY}(\mathbf Z/p)\) with witness \(W=\sigma\), \[ \boxed{\,R^{(p)}_\sigma(z)=\frac{1-(p-1)z^2}{1-p\,z^2}\,},\qquad m_0=1,\ \ m_{2k+1}=0,\ \ m_{2k}=p^{\,k-1}\ (k\ge1), \] with fusion characteristic polynomial \(\lambda^{\,p-1}(\lambda^2-p)\) and witness spectrum \(\{\sqrt p,-\sqrt p\}\). The resolvent denominator returns the metaplectic prime, \(p=\operatorname{coeff}_{z^2}\big[\!\operatorname{denom}R^{(p)}_\sigma\big]\). dlp_metaplectic_witness_verify.py; independent rebuild for \(p=5,7,11,13\)

The bare TY category is a fusion category; its modular completion is the odd metaplectic category \(SO(p)_2\) of Ardonne–Cheng–Rowell–Wang, with invertibles \(\mathbf 1,Z\), two objects \(X_1,X_2\) of dimension \(\sqrt p\), and \((p-1)/2\) objects \(Y_i\) of dimension \(2\). imported Here \(Z\) is a boson, and condensing it returns \(\operatorname{TY}(\mathbf Z/p)\) with \(X_1,X_2\mapsto\sigma\) and \(\mathbf 1,Z\mapsto\mathbf 1\). The condensation leaves a precise footprint in the witness moments.

\(SO(p)_2\) split-resolvent and the exact \(Z\)-footprintVerified · fusion-level

For the \(SO(p)_2\) witness \(W=X_1\), \[ \boxed{\,R^{SO(p)_2}_{X_1}(z)=\frac{1-p\,z^2+\tfrac{p-1}{2}z^4}{(1-z^2)(1-p\,z^2)}\,},\qquad m_{2k}=\frac{p^{\,k-1}+1}{2}, \] with characteristic polynomial \(\lambda^{(p-1)/2}(\lambda^2-1)(\lambda^2-p)\) and Perron value \(\sqrt p=\dim X_1\). The condensed and uncondensed witnesses are tied by an exact channel split: writing \(m_{\mathbf 1}=(N_{X_1}^{\,n})_{\mathbf 1\mathbf 1}\) and \(m_Z=(N_{X_1}^{\,n})_{Z\mathbf 1}\), \[ m_{\mathbf 1}(2k)+m_Z(2k)=p^{\,k-1}=m^{\operatorname{TY}}_\sigma(2k),\qquad m_{\mathbf 1}(2k)-m_Z(2k)=1. \] The vacuum channel exceeds the \(Z\)-channel by exactly one; the “\(+1\)” in the \(SO(p)_2\) moment is the condensed boson’s footprint, not a normalization. independent rebuild for \(p=5,7,11\); Perron \(=\sqrt p\)

Three conductors must be kept apart, and the value of the appendix is that it separates rather than collapses them. The fusion prime \(N^{\mathrm{fusion}}=p\), read from the resolvent denominator, is canonical at the Grothendieck-ring level and is verified. The modular twist-conductor \(N^{\mathrm{top}}=\operatorname{ord}\!\big(T|_{\mathrm{active}(W)}\big)\) is not determined by fusion alone: the ACRW classification builds odd metaplectic categories as gaugings of cyclic modular categories, with the twist data depending on a quadratic-form choice and an \(H^3(\mathbf Z_2;U(1))\) parameter, so \(N^{\mathrm{top}}\) is open until a modular lift is selected. Consequently the weld this appendix was reaching for — equality of the witness twist-conductor with the spine’s independently computed arithmetic conductor, \(N^{\mathrm{top}}\stackrel{?}{=}N_{\mathrm{arith}}\) — is taken up in Appendix DBD, where, on selecting the DAZ modular lift, it is resolved not as an equality but as a refinement: the relation \((ST)^3=\xi S^2\) pins the spinor twist and forces \(N^{\mathrm{top}}=p\cdot N_{\mathrm{frame}}\). What is settled is narrower and real: the witness resolvent is an exact finite invariant that reads the metaplectic prime and exposes the \(Z\)-condensation at the level of moments, with no claim of identity to the arithmetic-torsion objects certified elsewhere in the monograph.

The reach purchased by enlargement is an exact integer. The braid \(*\)‑algebra fills the charge‑graded algebra, \(\dim\langle\rho(B_n)\rangle=14=\dim\bigoplus_c M_{m_c}\), but sits strictly below the full matrix algebra \(M_D\) of dimension \(D^2=36\); the deficit \(D^2-\dim\langle\rho(B_n)\rangle=22\) is the charge‑violating part that braiding cannot reach. The charge projector is a non‑unitary idempotent outside the braid algebra, so measurement/projector enlargement strictly increases reach—adaptively, not by any static idempotent. This makes “measurement is forced” a quantitative statement.

RG·13 — A formal foothold

The fastest authority upgrade is arithmetic, not analytic. A Lean 4 nucleus, \(\texttt{ResidueGeometry.lean}\), states the RG·1 facts—\(\kappa(m,n)=\sum_p v_p(m)v_p(n)\), coprimality as orthogonality \(\kappa(m,n)=0\iff\gcd(m,n)=1\), bilinearity \(\kappa(mn,r)=\kappa(m,r)+\kappa(n,r)\), and the divisor‑count defect \(\tau(m)\tau(n)-\tau(mn)\ge0\) with equality iff coprime—against Mathlib, with the same \([\mathrm D]/[\mathrm K]/[\mathrm S]\) status discipline the conductor nucleus uses. It ships with a CI scaffold (\(\texttt{lakefile.toml}\), \(\texttt{lean-toolchain}\), a \(\texttt{lake build}\) workflow), so it kernel‑checks the moment it runs where the network is open. It is authored, not yet kernel‑checked here: the sandbox egress proxy blocks \(\texttt{lake build}\) and the Mathlib cache, the project's standing epistemic firewall, so RG·1 remains exact_finite with a kernel_checked‑pending lift on file.

RG·14 — Paper III: the analytic trace engine

The deepest unifier is analytic. For a defect \(\Delta=A-B\) between two operators, with resolvents \(R_M(z)=(zI-M)^{-1}\), the resolvent identity \(R_A-R_B=R_A\,\Delta\,R_B\) propagates by holomorphic functional calculus into a residue trace formula and a determinant ratio:

\[ \operatorname{Tr}f(A)-\operatorname{Tr}f(B)=\frac1{2\pi i}\oint_\Gamma f(z)\,\operatorname{Tr}\!\big(R_A(z)\,\Delta\,R_B(z)\big)\,dz,\qquad \log\frac{\det(zI-A)}{\det(zI-B)}=-\sum_{k\ge1}\frac1k\operatorname{Tr}\!\big((R_B(z)\Delta)^k\big). \]
Witness RG·14Verified
All four identities—resolvent, residue trace (for \(f=z^3\) and \(f=e^z\), by contour integration on a circle enclosing both spectra), determinant ratio, and the log‑determinant (Plemelj‑Smithies) expansion—are verified to machine precision. The spectral difference is literally the trace of the comparison defect: a repair primitive \(R_A(z)\Delta R_B(z)\) whose contour trace recovers \(\operatorname{Tr}f(A)-\operatorname{Tr}f(B)\).

The arithmetic collision zeta is the same law over the prime spectrum. Because \(Z_t=\prod_pL_p(p^{-s},e^t)\), the log‑ratio is a sum—a trace—of local defect logs, \(\log\!\frac{Z_t(s)}{Z_0(s)}=\sum_p\log\frac{L_p(p^{-s},e^t)}{L_p(p^{-s},1)}\), verified against RG·2 (here \(\sum_p=-0.040211\) matching \(\log Z_t-\log Z_0=-0.040211\) at \(s=2,\ t=-\tfrac12\)). So the arithmetic residue constant \(H_t(1)\), the categorical \([\omega]\), the braid reach deficit, and an operator spectral difference are five readings of one residue‑trace law.

The governing claimFramework
To know an object is to know its comparison profile. An integer is a valuation vector whose multiplication creates collision residues; a fusion ring is a positivity‑sensitive Galois object; a braid representation is a projected dynamical system with leakage cohomology; a category is a repair environment for coherence defects; a theorem is a certificate that a defect is zero, exact, or obstructive. Across all of them the same sentence holds: an invariant is the trace of the minimal repair that turns a closed non‑exact comparison defect into a boundary, \[ \mathfrak I(X)=\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathcal E}(h),\qquad Dh=\Delta_X,\qquad [\Delta_X]_{\mathcal C}\ne0,\quad[\Delta_X]_{\mathcal E}=0. \]Residue Geometry is the discipline of computing that trace.
